title: Latency fingerprinter: route+model streaming vs non-streaming breakdown with tracing hooks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a 'latency fingerprinter' pipeline and dashboarding primitives that reliably decompose P50/P95/P99 latency by route and model while splitting streaming vs non-streaming IO modes. Deliverables: tracing hook changes, metric extraction rules, aggregated histograms, and a Console dashboard that surface root-cause signals for regressions and rollout comparisons.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks added to runtime with an 'io_mode' attribute (stream|sync) and consistent route/model tags
Metrics pipeline produces per-route+model histograms for token Latinency that support p50/p95/p99 queries without per-request reaggregation cost
Console dashboard with selector for route, model, time window, and IO mode that shows p50/p95/p99 and sample traces linked to filtered traces
Low-overhead instrumentation: <3% tail latency overhead on production QPS in canary, verified via load test
Rollout plan and alerting: SLO alerts for p95 increase and automated regression report per-deploy
technical_approach: Tracing: extend OpenTelemetry span attributes at the invocation entry to include 'route_id', 'model_id', 'io_mode', 'cache_hit' and 'batch_size'. Add a small typed header so downstream services can preserve route/model context.

Metric extraction: emit per-token and per-request latency histograms from the runtime; aggregate via our metrics pipeline to produce daily/rolling histograms keyed by (route, model, io_mode, region, release). Use TDigest-like compression or Prometheus HDR histograms where appropriate.

Storage & rollup: short-term high-cardinality data (last 7d) in Cortex/Prometheus with series for route+model+io_mode; long-term aggregated rollups (30/90d) in ClickHouse as pre-computed histogram buckets for quick pXX computation.
Trace linking: add trace_id links in the dashboard; pre-filtered trace sample streams (1 in 200 by default, adjustable by error/latency) persist to Tempo/Jaeger for drilldown.

Dashboard UX: build a 'fingerprinter' panel with waterfall decomposition: total latency -> runtime queuing -> token generation -> network serialization, with IO-mode split toggles and comparison mode across releases or routes.
Safe rollout: feature-flag the new attributes and metric emission; canary in a 2% traffic slice, compare baseline metrics for 48h before ramp.
Cost controls: cap high-cardinality label explosion by enforcing route/model tag allowlist and coarse-grain model family fallback for low-volume routes.
tradeoffs: High-cardinality tags give better signal but increase metric ingestion cost — mitigated with allowlist and rollup into model-family buckets.
Sampling traces reduces storage but can miss rare tail cases; adaptive sampling for >p99 and errors compensates for this.
Using HDR histograms in Prometheus is efficient for pXX but requires careful bucket configs; ClickHouse rollups give faster long-range queries at the cost of extra ETL.
Adding io_mode to spans is simple but requires downstream preservation across proxies and gateways; we plan to use a typed header to avoid loss.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): feature-flag spans and metric tags in runtime on dedicated-canary pool (2% traffic) for 48h. Collect overhead metrics and error rate comparisons.
Phase 2 (observability pipeline): deploy extractor and rollup jobs to staging, validate histogram parity with raw samples, and add dashboard panels in Console staging.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): 10% -> 50% -> 100% over one week if canary shows <0.5% overhead and no SLO regressions.
Phase 4 (cleanup): remove temporary debug sampling once steady-state sampling verified and update docs/SDKs.
